Both routes visit the same nodes but use different edges, so two edge paths are returned: [1, 3] in the accent color and [2, 3] in teal; both share edge 3." width="100%"} Like `all_simple_paths()`, but each path is given by its edges rather than its nodes, so parallel edges produce distinct paths: two flights on the same route, two cables between the same racks, or two reactions linking the same metabolites are told apart. A path never visits a node twice. Edge direction is followed on directed graphs. The number of simple paths can grow exponentially; use `cutoff=` to bound their length. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The endpoints, as IDs or labels. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The endpoints, as IDs or labels. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum number of edges per path. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Each path as the list of its edge IDs, in travel order. Empty when `source` and `target` are the same node. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Depth-first search over edges with the current path's nodes blocked, as in NetworkX's `all_simple_edge_paths` (which yields `(u, v, key)` triples on multigraphs). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two parallel links from A to B, then one to C, give two distinct edge paths: ::: {#f607c9ac .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) g.all_simple_edge_paths("A", "C") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [[1, 3], [2, 3]] ``` ::: :::
